primitives.name: Local Stability Criterion
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model **Local stability.** Committee W_k of size k is **γ-approximately locally stable** if max_{a∉W_k} Pr_{i∼D}[a ≻_i W_k] ≤ γ/k (a ≻_i W_k = user i prefers a to *every* model in W_k).

primitives.assumptions: Users have strict preference orders; committee selection must satisfy approximate stability for all subsets.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When γ approaches zero, the system becomes overly restrictive; when γ is large, representation fails.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of pluralistic leaderboards lies in recognizing that Bradley-Terry models fail under heterogeneous user preferences. When two distinct preference profiles yield identical pairwise comparisons, a single scalar quality metric cannot capture the full spectrum of user values. Local stability addresses this by requiring that no alternative significantly preferred by a substantial fraction of users is excluded from top-k rankings. This is formalized through a probabilistic constraint on the likelihood that an outsider beats all members of a committee. The geometric checkpoint mechanism extends this idea into a scalable algorithmic framework where committees grow logarithmically, ensuring that each prefix maintains stability. The key innovation is that instead of aggregating all data into one ranking, the method constructs a hierarchy of committees that reflect diverse preferences. In GSE, this translates to evaluating current pick sheets for subgroup exclusion and implementing dynamic committee-based ranking updates that preserve fairness. The failure mode occurs when a consensus ranking excludes a coherent group—this manifests as a violation of the local stability condition, detectable through empirical testing of user preference distributions against top-k prefixes.
